requirement: Habeas MUST bundle a skill for deriving initial requirements from an existing codebase. The skill MUST direct agents to read the code and tests, map every first-party test to at least one requirement or example, identify and map every source unit implementing end-user-visible functionality or interactions to a requirement, and report gaps rather than claim complete coverage without an independent inventory review.
rationale:
I found no gap against `requirements.cli.bootstrap_skill`.

**Bundling.** `assets/skills/habeas-bootstrap-requirements/SKILL.md` is the `{impl}` item, declared by the `:impl:` option on the requirement. `Cargo.toml` registers `assets/skills` as a Symposium skills source, so the skill ships with Habeas. The test `bootstrap_skill_is_bundled_and_directs_complete_inventories` checks that `SKILLS` lists the skill, and the helper `skill_files` embeds the file with `include_str!`.

**Obligations, mapped to the skill text:**
- **Read the code and tests.** Workflow step 2 says "Read the existing requirements, documentation, public entry points, implementation, and tests. Follow behavior through the code rather than relying on test names or top-level dispatch."
- **Map every first-party test to at least one requirement or example.**
  - The Inventories section lists "every first-party runnable test or test case, including integration tests and parameterized cases".
  - The Tagging section says "Every test must end up with a `{test}` reference to a requirement or example". A test whose behavior no agreed requirement states goes on the gap list.
- **Identify and map every source unit implementing end-user-visible functionality.**
  - The Inventories section lists "every function, method, struct, enum, and union, listed from the source rather than from validation's uncovered items". It adds by hand the public APIs, commands, handlers, UI actions, configuration, outputs, errors and distinct observable branches.
  - It warns that a tagged entry point does not mean every branch beneath it has a requirement.
  - Tagging says to give roots their `{impl}` references and to "Map each other inventoried item to the requirement whose root reaches it".
- **Report gaps and not claim completeness without an independent review.**
  - Workflow step 8 has a fresh subagent recount both inventories without the lists.
  - The Report template includes "Independent recount" and a `Gaps:` list in the form `- <item or behavior> (<file>:<line>): <reason>; <open question>`.
  - It says "Claim 100% only when both inventories have no unmapped items, the independent recount agrees, and every observable branch has been reviewed. Don't silently exclude difficult cases."

**Tests.** The test carries `{test}` for the requirement. It runs the helpers `assert_phrases` and `assert_in_order`, which search the whitespace-collapsed `SKILL.md` and fail if a phrase is missing or out of order. It asserts phrases for each of the four obligations, plus the ordering of recount, gap-line format, the 100% condition, and not silently excluding cases. The skill's behavior is its text, so these phrase assertions are the appropriate test.

I found no unspecified extra behavior in the skill that conflicts with the text.
